question: Should OpenClaw ship an enabled-by-default bundled dashboard plugin that serves approval-pinned agent-authored widget assets through an unauthenticated sandboxed iframe route?
rationale: This creates a permanent browser code-execution and approval boundary; implementation correctness and green CI cannot substitute for explicit maintainer ownership of that product and security posture.

options.title: Ship after proof
options.body: Accept the boundary after all blockers are fixed and exact-head browser proof covers approval, pinned serving, navigation containment, rejection, revocation, and prompt sending.

options.title: Built-ins first
options.body: Land the workspace and trusted built-in widgets while deferring custom widgets to a focused security-reviewed change.

options.title: Require opt-in
options.body: Keep custom widgets behind an explicit experimental or opt-in gate rather than enabling the plugin surface by default.

recommendation.title: Ship after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the boundary after all blockers are fixed and exact-head browser proof covers approval, pinned serving, navigation containment, rejection, revocation, and prompt sending.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the integration and hardening sequence and have the strongest merged-history connection to the affected plugin and Control UI boundaries.
